summary: Defines the Single Rate Three Color Marker, a meter used in Diffserv traffic conditioners. It measures a packet stream against a committed rate and burst allowances, then marks each packet green, yellow or red to show how well it conforms. Routers can then treat the colors differently. This is an informational memo.

eli5.summary: Think of a traffic light for data. Each packet gets a green, yellow or red sticker depending on whether it fits the allowed speed, so busy roads can decide who goes first.

subtitle: A two-bucket meter that tags each packet green, yellow or red depending on how well it fits an agreed rate and burst size.

tldr.problem: A Diffserv network needs a standard way to measure a packet stream against an agreed rate and burst allowance, and to flag packets that go beyond it.
tldr.mechanism: The srTCM runs two token buckets that refill at one Committed Information Rate. A packet that fits in the committed bucket is green, one that fits only in the excess bucket is yellow, and anything else is red.
tldr.outcome: The colors are written into the DS field so routers can treat conforming and excess packets differently. The RFC is informational and sets no Internet standard.

facts.label: CIR unit
facts.value: Bytes of IP packets per second

today: RFC 2697 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its companion for two rates is RFC 2698.

sections.title: What the Marker Does
sections.content:
RFC 2697 defines the Single Rate Three Color Marker (srTCM), a component for a Diffserv traffic conditioner (see RFC 2475 and RFC 2474). It is split into a Meter, which measures each packet, and a Marker, which colors it using the Meter's result.

A packet is green if it does not exceed the Committed Burst Size (CBS), yellow if it exceeds the CBS but not the Excess Burst Size (EBS), and red otherwise. The RFC says this is useful for ingress policing of a service where only the length of a burst, not the peak rate, decides eligibility.

The Meter has two modes. In Color-Blind mode it assumes the stream has no colors yet. In Color-Aware mode some earlier entity has already colored each packet. How that pre-coloring is done is specific to the DS domain and outside the scope of the RFC.
sections.eli5: A checker watches packets go by and tells a painter which color to paint each one. If the packets are already painted, the checker can take that into account.

sections.title: Configuration Parameters
sections.content:
An srTCM is configured with its mode and three traffic parameters: the Committed Information Rate (CIR), the Committed Burst Size (CBS) and the Excess Burst Size (EBS).

The CIR is measured in bytes of IP packets per second, so it counts the IP header but not link-specific headers. CBS and EBS are measured in bytes. At least one of them must be larger than 0, and the RFC recommends that a nonzero value be at least the size of the largest possible IP packet in the stream.
sections.eli5: You set how fast packets may flow on average, and how big a sudden rush you will allow in two stages: a normal rush and an extra rush.

sections.title: How Metering Works
sections.content:
The Meter is described with two token buckets, C and E, that share the rate CIR. Bucket C holds at most CBS tokens and bucket E at most EBS. Both start full: Tc(0) = CBS and Te(0) = EBS.

Tokens are added CIR times per second. If Tc is below CBS, Tc goes up by one. Otherwise, if Te is below EBS, Te goes up by one. Otherwise nothing is added. So the excess bucket only fills once the committed bucket is full.

In Color-Blind mode, a packet of B bytes arriving at time t is green if Tc(t) - B >= 0, and Tc drops by B. Else it is yellow if Te(t) - B >= 0, and Te drops by B. Else it is red and neither bucket changes. In Color-Aware mode, a packet can only be green if it was pre-colored green, and it can only be yellow if it was pre-colored green or yellow, with the same token checks.

Coloring a packet needs enough tokens for the whole packet. The RFC chose this so that the volume of green packets is never smaller than the CIR and CBS imply, because tokens of a color are only spent on packets of that color. An implementation does not have to be built like this model.
sections.eli5: Imagine two piggy banks filled by the same allowance. A packet pays with the first bank if it can afford it, then the second, and if neither has enough it gets a red sticker.

sections.title: Marking and a Service Example
sections.content:
The Marker records the Meter's result by setting the DS field of the packet to a particular codepoint. With the Assured Forwarding PHB (RFC 2597), the color can be coded as the packet's drop precedence.

The RFC gives one example service: discard all red packets because they exceeded both burst sizes, forward yellow packets as best effort, and forward green packets with a low drop probability. A companion memo, RFC 2698, describes a Two Rate Three Color Marker where packets are marked based on two rates and two burst sizes.

On security, the RFC says only that the srTCM has no known security concerns.
sections.eli5: The color is written on the packet's label. Later, a router can throw away red ones first and let green ones through safely.
